{{Short description|American mathematician (1893–1960)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Claiborne Green Latimer''' (1893–1960) was an American mathematician, known for the [[Latimer–MacDuffee theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=A Correspondence Between Classes of Ideals and Classes of Matrices|author=Claiborne Latimer|authorlink2=Cyrus Colton MacDuffee|author2=C. C. MacDuffee|journal=The Annals of Mathematics|year=1933|volume=34|issue=2|pages=317–338|jstor=1968204|doi=10.2307/1968204}}</ref>

==Career==
Latimer earned his PhD in 1924 from the [[University of Chicago]] under [[Leonard Dickson]] with thesis ''Arithmetic of Generalized Quaternion Algebras''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6100}}</ref> He was an assistant professor at [[Tulane University]] for 2 years,<ref>{{cite journal|title=none<!-- unknown -->|journal=Farmers Advocate|date=June 4, 1927|page=1|location=Charles Town, West Virginia}}</ref> before becoming a mathematics professor at the [[University of Kentucky]] in 1927. After 20 years at the University of Kentucky, he resigned in 1947 and became a professor at [[Emory University]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Dr. Latimer Resigns|journal=Farmers Advocate|date=April 4, 1947|page=5|location=Charles Town, West Virginia}}</ref> Latimer was an amateur photographer; some of his photographs are preserved in the archives of the University of Kentucky and Emory University.<ref>[http://www.edwardfisk.com/lexington.html Edward Fisk from edwardfisk.com]</ref>
